_about: Topic 52 summary page (replaces the ch52-summary video). Content = the topic-52 scripts (math_patches/_ai_vis_t52.py), the Hebrew lessons (charts subtitles seg01-seg11) and the memory card mem-ch52-chart-types. Build: python3 summary_pages.py 52. The chart data are the course's own.
intro: Every quantitative section has **one chart or one table** with $4$ or $5$ questions (about $5$ to $6$ minutes). Spend the **first $1$ to $1\frac12$ minutes on the page**: the explanation, **the example checked in the chart**, the units, the key and every note. Charts are **drawn exactly to scale**, so most questions are solved **by eye**.

head: Step
Example
rows: Check the example in the chart. It doesn't match? Read again slowly; still not? Leave the set for the end.
"In 2010, 60 thousand vehicles were sold": the 2010 bar reaches $60$
Units: thousands, hundreds, percent
$90$ on a thousands axis $=90{,}000$; $\;40$ on a percent axis $=40\%$
Every note is there for a reason
"The exact location of each shape is its centre"
The questions go from easy to hard; the first one pulls out one value
2011: $80$ thousand
A set at the start or the middle of the section: solve it when you reach it
it is usually easier than the questions around it

head: Type
How to read it
Its trap
rows: Table
the row and the column cross at the value
who is the whole? (after "of" comes the whole)
Points on axes
up from the category, across to the axis; the key says which mark
a Z on the axis: that part is not to scale
Line graph
values **only at the marked points**; the line shows the trend
there is no "2010 and a half"
Bar chart
the height is the value; bars can be side by side, inside each other, stacked, or horizontal
stacked: a part is **the gap** ($110-60=50$), not the top
Continuous line
**every** point of the line is a measurement
a steep slope from a high start is a small relative rise
Range chart
bottom $=$ lowest, top $=$ highest, the bold line $=$ the mean
the mean is not the middle of the bar
Regions chart
find the point of the two values; its area gives the answer
read the units of the numbers inside
Circle chart
a chart on axes bent round: the circles are the values
a dark area $=$ where **most** are, not all
Cumulative graph
each point $=$ everything up to it; one period $=$ this point $-$ the one before
the last point is the total, "up to June"
Change graph
each point $=$ the change from the period before
ignore the line, look only at the points

head: Tool
Example
rows: Count past a value: draw a line at it, count what is beyond; a point **on** the line is not more
more than $50$ thousand privately owned: only $2013$
Compare by eye: lengths, corners, slopes
the longest range line; the bottom right corner
A steeper line $=$ a bigger change
$+10$ vs $+15$: the steeper part
Mini-graphs as choices: check only where they differ, edges first
below $10\%$: $4$ samples
Most, least: the biggest income and the smallest cost

head: Topic
Example
rows: Average: the sum $\div$ how many (symmetric numbers: the middle)
Percent of the whole
Overlap: the four squares
A percent of a bar
Weighted average: nearer the heavier group

items: Reading the wrong axis (carbon or hydrogen?): circle the key word.
Your answer is not a choice: stop and check the axis, the key, the question.
A shape that touches the line: it counts at its centre.
Dividing by $5$ instead of $6$ years ($2017$ to $2022$ is $6$ years).
Shared guests belong to both sides; "and not from the groom's side" leaves them out.
